info.name: Gummies E-Commerce API
info.description:
API collection for the single-vendor gummy e-commerce backend (Express + PostgreSQL).

Run order matters for the numbered folders (0-14): earlier folders create resources (category, product, variant, order, ...) that later folders/requests depend on via collection variables. Use the Postman Collection Runner to execute top-to-bottom for a full smoke test, or run folders individually once the setup folders (0-5) have populated the shared IDs at least once.

Start by running "1. Auth > Login (Super Admin)" - every other authenticated request inherits its bearer token from the collection-level auth ({{accessToken}}).

Media uploads (folder 4) require manually selecting a file in the "file" form field before sending - Postman does not allow a portable collection to pre-fill a local file path.

exec: // Generated once per collection run and reused in fixture names/SKUs/emails
// below, so the collection can be re-run repeatedly (including against a
// database that already has the `npm run seed` demo data) without 409s.

request.description: Logs in as the seeded super admin and stores the access token for all subsequent authenticated requests. Also sets a refreshToken httpOnly cookie (Postman handles this automatically).
Uses the refreshToken cookie set by Login to rotate the access token. Requires Postman's cookie jar to have captured the cookie from the Login request (default behavior).
Revokes the refresh token. Run this last if you want to confirm the session is fully closed - re-run Login afterwards if you continue testing.
Logs in as the staff admin created above. Stored separately as {{staffAccessToken}} so it does not clobber the super admin session used elsewhere in the collection.
Select an image file for the "file" field before sending (Postman does not allow pre-filling a file path in a portable collection).

request.description: Returns the product with its active variants (including live availability) and images.
Creating a variant automatically creates its inventory record (initialQuantity units on hand).
Kept separate from the primary variant used by Inventory/Orders below, so the Cleanup folder can delete it without disturbing those flows.
Run "Upload Product Image" in the Media folder first so {{productImageMediaId}} is set.
Removes the image attachment only - the underlying media file is untouched (see Cleanup folder to delete it).
No auth required - this is the public guest checkout endpoint. Reserves stock for {{variantId}} inside a DB transaction; run "Add Variant (Primary)" first.
Public lookup by order number + the email used at checkout - no admin auth needed.
Transitioning to "shipped" fulfills the reservation: on-hand and reserved quantities both decrease by the ordered amount.
Demonstrates the order status state machine rejecting an illegal transition.
Run "Create Order (Guest Checkout)" first - guest checkout upserts a customer record by email.

Confirms stock reservation correctly rejects an order that exceeds available inventory, and rolls back the whole transaction.
Admins are deactivated, not hard-deleted - there is no DELETE /admins endpoint by design.
Cascades deletion of the primary variant, its inventory record, and any attached product images.
